title: Bekhorot 49
description: How two fathers recover redemption money from one priest, why a son who dies within thirty days needs no redemption, whether a father may redeem his son before the thirtieth day, who comes first when a man must redeem both himself and his son, and which coins make up the five sela.

a2.he: וְהָאָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: לָא כָּתְבִינַן אַדְרַכְתָּא אַמִּטַּלְטְלִי! הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּכַפְרֵיהּ, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא כַּפְרֵיהּ — כָּתְבִינַן.

a3.he: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם. תָּנָא רַב הוּנָא: שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם.

a4.he: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן, כֵּיוָן דְּבִשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים הוּא דְּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ — לָא מִתְּנֵי לֵיהּ.

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ מֵת הַבֵּן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּתַן לַכֹּהֵן — יַחְזִיר. לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן — יִתֵּן. מֵת בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — כְּיוֹם שֶׁלְּפָנָיו. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אִם נָתַן — לֹא יִטּוֹל, וְאִם לֹא נָתַן — לֹא יִתֵּן.

a6.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן? גָּמְרִי ״חֹדֶשׁ״ ״חֹדֶשׁ״ מִמִּדְבָּר, מָה הָתָם ״וָמַעְלָה״ אַף הָכָא נָמֵי וָמַעְלָה.

a7.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ, מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״וָמַעְלָה״ גַּבֵּי עֲרָכִין, וְלָא גָּמְרִי מִמִּדְבָּר — הָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד,

a8.he: וְכׇל שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד — אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.

a9.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כִּי אֵין מְלַמְּדִין — לְעָלְמָא, אֲבָל לְגוּפַיְיהוּ — מְלַמְּדִין, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ.

a10.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים לְעִנְיַן אֲבֵילוּת, יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים כְּיוֹם שֶׁלְּפָנָיו. וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמֵּיקֵל בְּאֵבֶל.

a11.he: מַתְנִי׳ מֵת הָאָב בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים — בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדָּה, עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁנִּפְדָּה; לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁנִּפְדָּה, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדָּה. הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת — הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ; רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנוֹ קוֹדְמוֹ, שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ עַל אָבִיו וּמִצְוַת בְּנוֹ עָלָיו.

a12.he: גְּמָ׳ אִיתְּמַר: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, רַב אָמַר: בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי. דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא ״מֵעַכְשָׁיו״ — אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי, לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם וְאִיתַנְהוּ לְמָעוֹת — וַדַּאי בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי.

a13.he: כִּי פְּלִיגִי לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְנִתְעַכְּלוּ הַמָּעוֹת, רַב אָמַר: בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַקִּידּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה, הָתָם לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּנִתְעַכְּלוּ הַמָּעוֹת — הָווּ קִידּוּשֵׁי,

b2.he: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר לָךְ: הָתָם — בְּיָדוֹ לְקַדְּשָׁהּ מֵעַכְשָׁיו, הָכָא — אֵין בְּיָדוֹ לִפְדּוֹתוֹ מֵעַכְשָׁיו. וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַיְימָא לַן, דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דִּפְלִיגִי רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל — הִלְכְתָא כְּרַב בְּאִיסּוּרֵי וְכִשְׁמוּאֵל בְּדִינֵי, הָכָא הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.

b3.he: תְּנַן: מֵת בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּתַן לַכֹּהֵן — יַחְזִיר לוֹ חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים. טַעְמָא דְּמֵת, הָא לֹא מֵת — בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי! הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? דְּאִיתַנְהוּ לְמָעוֹת.

b4.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדָּה עַד שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ שֶׁנִּפְדָּה! הָתָם נָמֵי דְּאִיתַנְהוּ לְמָעוֹת בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ.

b5.he: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי?! וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַיְימָא לַן כְּרַב בְּאִיסּוּרֵי וְכִשְׁמוּאֵל בְּדִינֵי, הָכָא הִלְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.

b6.he: הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת — הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת — הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנוֹ קוֹדְמוֹ, שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ עַל אָבִיו, וּמִצְוַת בְּנוֹ עָלָיו.

b7.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים — הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּמִצְוָה דִּידֵיהּ עֲדִיף. כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא חָמֵשׁ מְשׁוּעְבָּדוֹת וְחָמֵשׁ בְּנֵי חוֹרִין.

b8.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה — כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, וְדִידֵיהּ אָזֵיל וְטָרֵיף מִמְּשַׁעְבְּדִי, וּבְהָנֵי חָמֵשׁ בְּנֵי חוֹרִין — פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ.

b9.he: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה — לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, הִלְכָּךְ מִצְוָה דִּידֵיהּ עָדִיף.

b10.he: מַתְנִי׳ חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים שֶׁל בֵּן — בְּמָנֶה צוֹרִי.

b11.he: שְׁלֹשִׁים שֶׁל עֶבֶד, חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁל אוֹנֵס וְשֶׁל מְפַתֶּה, וּמֵאָה שֶׁל מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע — כּוּלָּם בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ, בְּמָנֶה צוֹרִי. וְכוּלָּן נִפְדִּין בְּכֶסֶף וּבְשָׁוֵה כֶּסֶף, חוּץ מִשְּׁקָלִים.

b12.he: גְּמָ׳ מָנֶה צוֹרִי. אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: מָנֶה שֶׁל צוֹר. רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר: דִּינָרָא (ערבא) [עַרְבָיָא]. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר: אִיסְתֵּרָא סֻרְסְיָא דְּמִיזְדַּבְּנָא תְּמָנְיָא בְּדִינָרָא, חֲמֵשׁ מִינַּיְיהוּ לְפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן.

messages.text: Continued from 48b. The mishna ruled that if two fathers whose sons were intermingled gave all ten sela to one priest and one son died within thirty days, the priest returns five. The Gemara objected that the priest can turn each father away in turn, telling each that his own son is the one still alive. Shmuel answers:

This is referring to a case where one of the fathers comes with authorization to act on behalf of the other father to state his claim for him, and therefore the priest cannot reject his claim. But if they gave the money to two different priests an authorization is of no effect, as each priest can claim the other took the redemption money of the son who died.

notes.he: שני האבות כתבו הרשאה האחד לחבירו ובא בעל הרשאה ותובעו ממה נפשך אם שלי מת החזיר לי את שלי ואם של חבירי מת החזיר לי את שלו שהרי יש לי הרשאה:
notes.en: Comes with an authorization: the two fathers wrote authorizations, each to the other, and the holder of the authorization comes and claims from him: Whichever way you look at it, if mine died, return mine to me; and if my fellow’s died, return his to me, since I hold his authorization.

messages.text: But didn’t the Sages of Neharde’a say: We do not write an authorization document [adrakhta] concerning movable property? Therefore, in the case of redemption, where money, which has the status of movable property, is demanded from the priest, an authorization document may not be used.

notes.he: הרשאה אמטלטלי דהואיל ואינן בעין מיחזי כשיקרא שמא אין בידו משל זה כלום וחתימי סהדי אשיקרא:
notes.en: Adrakhta: an authorization. [We do not write one] for movable property: since it is not at hand, it looks like a lie. Perhaps he holds nothing of this man’s at all, and the witnesses would be signing a lie.

notes.he: תימה דללישנא קמא במרובה (ב"ק דף ע.) דלא מפליג בין כפריה ללא כפריה מאי איכא למימר וכן יש להקשות ממתני' פרק שבועת העדות (שבועות דף לג:) גבי איש פלוני כהן איש פלוני לוי דדייק הא מנה לפלוני ביד פלוני חייבין והא אמרת עד שישמע מפי תובע ומשני בבא בהרשאה ופריך והא אמרי נהרדעי כו' ה"מ היכא דכפריה כו' ומיהו ההוא איכא לאוקומי בפקדון ללישנא קמא דנהרדעי דכיון שיכול להקדיש בפקדון כדמוכח בפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פח.) גבי ההוא דאייתי קרי לפום נהרא ה"נ יכול להרשות דחד טעמא הוא כדמוכח ויש לתרץ הך דשמעתין [בקרקעות] ואליבא [דרבי] דאית ליה לקמן בפירקין (בכורות דף נא.) פודין בקרקעות כמו שפודין במטלטלי דאמקרקעי כתבינן אדרכתא דאמטלטלי דוקא לא כתבינן דאינו ברשותו אי נמי איכא לאוקמה כרבי נתן דמדרבי נתן יכול להוציא מידו אם חבירו חייב ואין לו מה לפרוע אי נמי איכא לאוקמה כגון שנתן אחד לחבירו במעמד שלשתן ומיהו צריך עיון דלמא היכא דאין יכול להוציא מידו בבית דין לא תקון רבנן מעמד שלשתן כי היכי דלא תקון מעמד שלשתן בכתובה משום דלא ניתנה לגבות מחיים כדפרישית בהחובל (ב"ק דף פט.) ועוד יש לתרץ דדלמא אם שניהם מצויים לפנינו ומצווים לתת לאחר חייב להחזיר ולא הוצרך להעמיד בבא בהרשאה אלא כדי שיוכל האחד להוציא מידו בפני עצמו:
notes.en: In brief: [On “That applies where he denied it.”] Tosafot ask what one can say according to the first version in Merubba (Bava Kamma 70a), which does not distinguish between a respondent who denied and one who did not. They ask the same from Shevuat HaEdut (Shevuot 33b), where the Gemara asks how “a maneh of so-and-so is in so-and-so’s hand” can be claimed by another, answers “where he comes with an authorization,” objects from the Nehardeans, and answers “that applies where he denied it.” That passage can be set in a deposit, even according to the first version: since a deposit can be consecrated (Bava Batra 88a, the man who brought gourds to the river bank), one can also authorize another to claim it, for it is one reason. For our passage they offer several answers: it may speak of land and follow Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who holds below (51a) that one may redeem with land, and for land an authorization is written; or it follows Rabbi Natan, by whose rule one may take from a debtor’s debtor; or one father gave the other his claim in the presence of all three. This last needs examination, since the Rabbis may not have instituted “the presence of all three” where the claim cannot be collected in court, just as they did not for a ketuba (see Bava Kamma 89a). Finally: perhaps when both fathers are present and tell the priest to pay, he must return the money, and the authorization was needed only so that one father could recover it alone. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: הרשאה:
notes.en: Adrakhta: an authorization.

messages.text: This statement, that one does not write authorization for movable property, applies only when the respondent, in this case the priest, already denied the claim against him. But in a case where the respondent did not yet deny the claim against him we write authorization even for movable property. In the case of redemption, although the priest claims the one issuing the claim against him is not the father of the son who died, he does not deny that he received the money.

notes.he: לוה למלוה תו לא כתב מלוה הרשאה עלייהו משום דמיחזי כשיקרא:
notes.en: Where he denied it: [where] the borrower [denied the debt] to the lender, the lender can no longer write an authorization for it, because it looks like a lie.

notes.he: מה שנוהגים עכשיו לכתוב הרשאה אפילו כפריה אומר ר"ת דהיינו טעמא דלא כתבינן לנהרדעי היינו משום דמחזי כשיקרא כדאמרי' במרובה (ב"ק ע.) ובכתובות (דף פה.) מוכח דלמיחזי כשיקרא לא חיישינן ובמרובה [שם ד"ה אמטלטלין] הארכתי:
notes.en: But where he did not deny it we write: As for our practice nowadays of writing an authorization even where he denied it, Rabbeinu Tam says that the Nehardeans’ reason for not writing one is that it looks like a lie, as we say in Merubba (Bava Kamma 70a); and in Ketubot (85a) it is evident that we are not concerned about “looking like a lie.” I have discussed this at length in Merubba [ibid., s.v. amitaltelin].

notes.he: משום דמיחזי כשיקרא:
notes.en: Where he denied it: because it looks like a lie.

messages.text: With regard to two women who had not previously given birth who were married to two men, and gave birth to a male and a female who then became intermingled, the fathers are exempt from the mitzva of redemption but the son is obligated to redeem himself, as he certainly has firstborn status. If the offspring were two females and a male, or two males and two females, all of whom became intermingled, the priest has nothing here.

If they gave birth to two males and a female the priest has nothing here, despite the fact that one of them is definitely a firstborn, as each father can claim that his firstborn is the female. In addition, the sons are exempt as well, since each can claim that the female was his sister and born first.
messages.lead: Concerning this case, Rav Huna teaches:

notes.he: גבי שתי נשים של ב' אנשים שלא בכרו וילדו שני זכרים ונקבה במחבא אין כאן לכהן כלום ואע"ג דחד הוי בכור ממ"נ דאם האחת ילדה ב' זכרים האחד בכור ואם זכר ונקבה ילדה נמצאת חבירתה יולדת זכר לבדו והוא בכור ואפ"ה הבן אינו חייב לפדות את עצמו דא"ל שמא אין אני בכור אלא חבירי:
notes.en: Rav Huna teaches: concerning two women of two men who had not given birth and who bore, unobserved, two males and a female, the priest has nothing here. And this is so even though one of them is a firstborn whichever way you look at it: if one woman bore the two males, one of them is a firstborn; and if she bore a male and a female, her fellow turns out to have borne a male alone, and he is a firstborn. Even so, the son is not obligated to redeem himself, for he can say to [the priest]: Perhaps I am not the firstborn, but my fellow is.

notes.he: מוסיף על מתניתי' דאחת בכרה ואחת שלא בכרה של ב' אנשים וילדו כו'. מוסיף ב' זכרים ונקבה אין כאן לכהן כלום דמצי אמר מי שלא בכרה אשתו דלמא איתתי יליד זכר ונקבה ואיני יודע איזה יצא ראשון:
notes.en: Rav Huna teaches: he adds to our mishna, [to the case of] one [wife] who had given birth and one who had not, of two men, who gave birth, etc. He adds: two males and a female, the priest has nothing here, for the one whose wife had not given birth can say: Perhaps my wife bore a male and a female, and I do not know which came out first. [Rabbeinu Gershom sets Rav Huna’s addition in the case of one woman who had given birth and one who had not; Rashi sets it in the case of two who had not.]

messages.text: And with regard to the tanna of our mishna, why does he not state this case?

Since you find this ruling that they are entirely exempt in a case where the women are married to two men, but you do not find it in a case of one man and two of his wives, as a firstborn was definitely born to that man and he must give five sela coins to a priest, the tanna does not teach the case of two women and two men either. The reason is that stylistically, the tanna prefers to teach the ruling: The priest has nothing here, only when the halakha is identical in a case of two wives of two men and a case of two wives of one man.

notes.dh: באיש אחד ושתי נשים לא משכחת לה
notes.he: דכיון דאיכא חד בכור יהיב ה' סלעים לכהן להכי לא תני ליה דכל הנך דתנא כאן אין כאן לכהן כלום שוין בין איש אחד ושתי נשיו בין בשתי נשים של שני אנשים:
notes.en: With one man and two women you do not find it: since there is certainly one firstborn, he gives five sela to the priest. That is why [the tanna] does not teach it, for all the cases in which he taught “the priest has nothing here” are the same whether for one man and his two wives or for two wives of two men.

notes.he: דלא תני לה דכיון דלא משכחת לה באיש ושתי נשיו שאחת ביכרה ואחת לא ביכרה דממה נפשך חייב בה' סלעים דהא ב' זכרים ילוד לא מיתני ליה:
notes.en: And our tanna [does not teach it]: because you do not find it with a man and his two wives, one who had given birth and one who had not, for whichever way you look at it he is liable for five sela, since two males were born. [So] he does not teach it.

messages.text: Mishna
If the firstborn son dies within thirty days of birth, although the father gave five sela to the priest, the priest must return it.

notes.he: אבכורות ודאין דעלמא קאי נמי:
notes.en: Mishna. If the son died within thirty: this refers also to ordinary, certain firstborns [not only to the intermingled ones above].

notes.he: דנפל הוה ולא מיחייב בפדיון עד לאחר שלשים:
notes.en: He must return: since it was a nefel [a nonviable birth], and he is not obligated in redemption until after thirty days.

notes.dh: מת בנו בתוך שלשים יום כו' יחזיר לו ה' סלעים
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס משום דנפל הוא ובחנם פירש כן דאפילו קים לן ביה דכלו לו חדשיו בבן חדש תלה רחמנא:
notes.en: If his son died within thirty days … he must return the five sela: The Kuntres [Rashi] explains: because he is a nefel. He explained so needlessly, for even if we know that his months were completed, the Merciful One made it depend on [his being] a month old.

notes.he: בבכור דכל אשה קא מיירי:
notes.en: If the son died within thirty: it speaks of the firstborn of any woman.

messages.text: If the firstborn son dies after thirty days have passed, even if the father did not give five sela coins to the priest he must give it then.

notes.dh: לאחר שלשים אע"פ שלא נתן יתן
notes.he: בפסחים בסופו (דף קכא:) אמרינן דאבי הבן מברך שתים ויש לספק כיון שמת אם מברך שהחיינו מכיון דזוכה לקיים המצוה ואין לתמוה אהא דלא מברכינן שהחיינו על כל מילה ומילה כמו על כל פדיון הבן דשאני מצות פדיון הבן דלא שכיחא:
notes.en: After thirty, even though he did not give, he must give: At the end of Pesaḥim (121b) we say that the father of the son recites two blessings. And there is room for doubt: since [the son] has died, does he recite “Who has kept us alive” [sheheḥeyanu], given that he merits to fulfill the mitzva? And one should not wonder why we do not recite sheheḥeyanu on every circumcision as on every redemption of the son, for the mitzva of redemption of the son is different, since it is uncommon.

messages.text: If the firstborn dies on the thirtieth day, that day’s halakhic status is like that of the day that preceded it, as the obligation takes effect only after thirty days have elapsed.

notes.he: אף ע"פ שנתן יחזיר לו:
notes.en: Like the day before it: even though he gave, [the priest] must return it to him.

notes.he: וא"ת דבריש החולץ (יבמות דף לז:) משמע דפשיטא לן מן התורה אפי' תוך ל' דחי הוא דאמר מת בתוך ל' ועמדה ונתקדשה אם אשת כהן היא אינה חולצת וי"ל דהתם בנפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי כרבנן דפליגי ארבן שמעון בן גמליאל בסוף ר"א דמילה אבל הכא בפיהק ומת דכולי עלמא מת הוא ומיהו אפ"ה איירי הכא בנפל מן הגג כי התם אין לחוש דהכי נמי פסקינן בסוף אם לא הביא כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל לענין אבילות להקל אף על גב דבאשת כהן דלא אפשר סמכינן אדרבנן ושריא בלא חליצה וא"ת דהכא מקילינן כל כך לענין אבילות אפילו באותו דחשבינן ודאי בר קיימא היכא דלא אפשר כגון באשת כהן ובמס' שמחות פ"ד (הל"ב) תנן הספקות אוננין ומתאבלין עליהן וי"ל דהתם בספק בן תשע לראשון או בן שבע לאחרון דגנאי הדבר שלא יתאבל לא זה ולא זה והרי הוא ודאי בנו של אחד מהן:
notes.en: Like the day before it: And if you say: at the start of HaḤoletz (Yevamot 37b) it seems we take it as obvious by Torah law that even within thirty he is alive, for it says: if he died within thirty and [his widow] was betrothed, if she is a priest’s wife she does not perform ḥalitza. One may answer that there it refers to one who fell from a roof or was eaten by a lion, according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel at the end of Rabbi Eliezer DeMila; but here it refers to one who yawned and died, where all agree he was a nefel. And even if it refers here to one who fell from a roof, as there, there is no difficulty, for we likewise rule at the end of Im Lo Hevi (Shabbat 136a) like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, to be lenient regarding mourning, even though for a priest’s wife, where there is no other way, we rely on the Rabbis and permit her without ḥalitza. And if you say: here we are so lenient regarding mourning even for one we treat as certainly viable where there is no other way, as with the priest’s wife; yet in tractate Semaḥot, chapter 4 (halakha 2), it is taught that for doubtful cases one acts as an onen and mourns. One may answer that there it refers to a doubt whether he is a nine-month child of the first [husband] or a seven-month child of the later one, for it would be disgraceful that neither this one nor that one mourn, and he is certainly the son of one of them.

notes.he: ופטור:
notes.en: Like the day before it: and he is exempt.

messages.text: If the firstborn dies on the thirtieth day it is a case of uncertainty; therefore, if the father already gave the redemption payment to the priest he cannot take it back, but if he did not yet give payment he does not need to give it.

notes.dh: מת ביום שלשים כיום שלפניו ר' עקיבא אומר כו'
notes.he: בריש החולץ (יבמות דף לו:) אמרינן התם תניא ר"ש בן גמליאל אומר כל ששהה ל' יום באדם אינו נפל הא לא שהה ספיקא הוי ואיתמר מת בתוך שלשים יום ועמדה ונתקדשה אם אשת ישראל היא חולצת וברוב הספרים גרסינן בסוף פרק רבי אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קלו.) מת ביום שלשים וכן גורס ר"י ור"ח גורס כן ונראה דגורס תוך שלשים דכיון דאמרי רבנן הכא יום שלשים כיום שלפניו ור"ח משוי ליה ספיקא ופליגי רבנן ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל גם ביום שלשים מה לי ביום שלשים ומה לי בתוך ל' יום גם בשאלתות גורס תוך שלשים ומיהו בהלכות גדולות כתוב דביום ל' אפילו פיהק ומת לא הוי נפל לרבנן ודוקא תוך שלשים הוא דאמרינן במסכת שבת פיהק ומת דברי הכל מת הוא משמע דגרסינן ביום שלשים ומפרשי מת כמשמעו פיהק ומת וקחשיב פיהק ומת ביום שלשים כיון שחי כל כך כנפל מן הגג תוך שלשים ועוד יש לקיים גירסא זו אם בנפל מן הגג ואכלו ארי ביום שלשים דוקא הוא דסמכינן אדרבנן ושמא אפי' לענין אבילות דהוי כבר קיימא:
notes.en: In brief: [On the thirtieth day and Rabbi Akiva.] At the start of HaḤoletz (Yevamot 36b) Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches that whatever has lived thirty days among humans is not a nefel, so short of that it is a doubt; and it was stated there: if [the child] died within thirty days and [the widow] was betrothed, if she is an Israelite’s wife she performs ḥalitza. At the end of Rabbi Eliezer DeMila (Shabbat 136a) most texts read “died on the thirtieth day,” and so the Ri reads. Rabbeinu Ḥananel apparently reads “within thirty”: since the Rabbis here hold the thirtieth day is like the day before and Rabbi Akiva holds it doubtful, if the Rabbis and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagreed even about the thirtieth day, what difference would there be between the thirtieth day and within thirty? The She’iltot also read “within thirty.” But Halakhot Gedolot write that on the thirtieth day, even one who yawned and died is not a nefel according to the Rabbis, and only within thirty does Shabbat say that if he yawned and died all agree he was a nefel. That implies the reading “on the thirtieth day,” taking “died” plainly as yawned and died: one who lived that long and yawned and died on the thirtieth day is treated like one who fell from a roof within thirty. The reading can also be kept if it means one who fell from a roof or was eaten by a lion on the thirtieth day specifically, where we rely on the Rabbis, perhaps even for mourning, that he was already viable. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Gemara
What is the reason of the Rabbis, i.e., the first tanna, who hold that the mitzva of redemption applies only after thirty days have elapsed?
messages.quote: dies on the thirtieth day, that day’s halakhic status is like that of the day that preceded it

messages.text: They derive the meaning of the term “month” stated in this context by means of a verbal analogy from the meaning of the term “month” stated in the context of the redemption of the Israelite firstborn in the wilderness via the Levites. Just as there, with regard to the redemption through the Levites, it is stated: “Number all the firstborn males of the children of Israel from a month old and upward” (Numbers 3:40), i.e., after thirty days, so too here, with regard to the mitzva of redemption for future generations, where it states: “From a month old you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:16), the requirement: And upward, applies as well, i.e., only after thirty days.

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה פְּקֹד כׇּל־בְּכֹר זָכָר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה וְשָׂא אֵת מִסְפַּר שְׁמֹתָם׃
verse.en: GOD said to Moses: Record every first-born male of the Israelite people from the age of one month up, and make a list of their names;

notes.he: כתיב הכא (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז) ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה וכתיב במדבר (שם ג) פקוד כל בכור זכר מבן חדש ומעלה:
notes.en: Gemara. From the wilderness: here it is written: “And those that are to be redeemed, from a month old shall you redeem” (Numbers 18:15–16), and of the wilderness it is written: “Number all the firstborn males … from a month old and upward” (Numbers 3:40).

notes.he: משמע לאחר שלשים:
notes.en: And upward: implies after thirty [days].

notes.he: במדבר כתי' ומעלה דהיינו שלשים ויותר חדש הוי כ"ט ימים ומחצה ומעלה הוי יום א' היינו ל' יום ומחצה והיינו (כל אחד) [לאחר ל'] ומשום הכי חייב אבל יום א' שלפניו ופטור:
notes.en: Just as there: of the wilderness “and upward” is written, meaning thirty and more. A month is twenty-nine and a half days, and “upward” is one day more, which makes thirty and a half days, that is, after thirty. Therefore if he died on the thirtieth day it is like the day before it, and he is exempt. [The last words of the note are garbled in the printed text.]

messages.text: And Rabbi Akiva is uncertain in this regard, as one could claim: From the fact that it was necessary for the verse to write “and upward” with regard to the mitzva of valuations: “And if it be from sixty years old and upward” (Leviticus 27:7), and it is not derived from the redemption of the Israelite firstborns in the wilderness that the phrase “from…years old” means “and upward,” one can conclude the following: The redemption of the firstborn in the wilderness and valuations are two verses that come as one, i.e., to teach the same matter.
messages.quote: it is a case of uncertainty

verse.he: וְאִם מִבֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה אִם־זָכָר וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שָׁקֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשָׂרָה שְׁקָלִים׃
verse.en: If the age is sixty years or over, the equivalent is fifteen shekels in the case of a male and ten shekels for a female.

notes.he: אי גמרי מהתם דמדאיצטריך ומעלה בערכין אם מבן ששים ומעלה וגו' וגמר במסכת ערכין (דף יח.) שנה שנה לג"ש שכשם ששנת ששים כלמטה הימנו להחמיר אף שנת חמש ושנת עשרים כלמטה אע"ג דלהקל והוא הדין לענין בן חדש דיום ל' כלמטה אע"ג דלהקל ולא גמר חדש חדש ממדבר דלא יהא נערך עד לאחר שלשים:
notes.en: He is uncertain whether we derive it from there. For since “and upward” was needed in valuations, “And if it be from sixty years old and upward,” and [the Gemara] in tractate Arakhin (18a) derives “year,” “year” by verbal analogy, that just as the sixtieth year is treated like the years below it, as a stringency, so too the fifth year and the twentieth year are treated like those below them, even though that is a leniency, the same applies to “a month old”: the thirtieth day is like the days below it, even though that is a leniency. And [Arakhin] does not derive “month,” “month” from the wilderness, that one would not be valuated until after thirty days.

notes.he: דערכין ודמדבר סיני שני כתובין הבאין כאחד ואין מלמדין על פדיון הבן:
notes.en: They are: [the verses] of valuations and of the wilderness of Sinai are two verses that come as one, and they do not teach about the redemption of the son.

notes.he: אי גמרינן דמדאיצטריך למיכתב ולמעלה גבי ערכין (משום דליהוו) [הוי להו] ב' כתובין באין כאחת:
notes.en: And Rabbi Akiva is uncertain whether we derive it: since it was necessary to write “and upward” with regard to valuations, they are two verses that come as one.

messages.text: And there is a principle that any two verses that come as one do not teach their common halakha to other cases. If so, the halakha with regard to the mitzva of redeeming the firstborn for future generations would be that the thirtieth day is like the following day, which is not in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

Or perhaps one could say: When do two verses that come as one not teach their common halakha? That is with regard to general halakhot, i.e., entirely different areas of halakha. But with regard to themselves, i.e., similar cases, they do teach. If so, one should derive permanent halakha of redemption of firstborns from the redemption of the firstborn in the wilderness. And it is due to that reason that Rabbi Akiva is uncertain concerning a firstborn on his thirtieth day.

notes.dh: או דלמא כי אמר אין מלמדין
notes.he: שני כתובין ה"מ לעלמא דלא משתעי מבכור ודערכין כמו אי הוה כתב חדש במידי אחרינא:
notes.en: Or perhaps, when we say that two verses do not teach, that applies to the world at large, to matters that do not speak of a firstborn or of valuations, as if “month” were written about some other matter.

notes.he: כגון בכורי דורות מבכורי מדבר דאידי ואידי בבכור הוא משתעי מלמדין ומדמספקא לן קאמר אם נתן לא יטול ואם לא נתן לא יתן:
notes.en: But for themselves: such as the firstborns of future generations from the firstborns of the wilderness, since both speak of a firstborn, they do teach. And because we are uncertain, he says: If he gave, he does not take it back; and if he did not give, he does not give.

notes.he: דחדש דמדבר דכתיב ביה ומעלה ופדויו מבן חדש תרוייהו בבכור אדם מישתעי ודלמא דמלמדין להכי מספקא ליה וקאמר ואם נתן לא יטול כו':
notes.en: But for themselves they do teach: for the “month” of the wilderness, of which “and upward” is written, and “those to be redeemed, from a month old,” both speak of a human firstborn. And perhaps they do teach; that is why he is uncertain, and says: If he gave, he does not take it back, etc.

messages.text: All concede with regard to mourning that the thirtieth day is like the preceding day, i.e., if the son died on the thirtieth day it is considered as though he died on the day before and he has the status of a stillborn, and the rites of mourning are not observed.

notes.he: אם מת ולד בתוך שלשים אין אבילות חלה על אביו דאימר נפל הוא:
notes.en: With regard to mourning: if a child dies within thirty [days], mourning does not take effect on his father, for one may say it was a nefel.

notes.he: דיום ל' כשל אחריו ומותר בגיהוץ ותספורת:
notes.en: That the thirtieth day is like the one after it, and he is permitted to launder his clothes and cut his hair. [Rabbeinu Gershom seems to read Rav Ashi’s ruling as concerning the thirty days of mourning, the thirtieth day counting as already past.]

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the more lenient authority in matters relating to mourning.
Mishna
If the father of the firstborn dies within thirty days of birth the presumptive status of the son is that he was not redeemed, until the son will bring proof that he was redeemed.

notes.he: דלא עביד איניש דפריק תוך שלשים עד שיביא ראיה:
notes.en: Mishna. That he was not redeemed: for people do not usually redeem within thirty [days]; [so he is presumed unredeemed] until he brings proof.

messages.text: If the father dies after thirty days have passed the presumptive status of the son is that he was redeemed, until people will tell him that he was not redeemed.

notes.he: דכהן הוי מוציא מחבירו והורע כחו:
notes.en: After thirty, the presumption is that he was redeemed: for the priest is the one seeking to take money from another, and his position is weaker.

notes.he: לבן שצוה אביו בשעת מיתתו שלא נפדה ובאמירה סגיא בלא עדות גמורה דהך חזקה דמחזקינן ליה בחזקת שנפדה לאו זו היא חזקה מעלייתא דרובא דאינשי לא עבדי למפרע חובו מיד והכא לא שייך למימר עד שיביא ראיה דהכא יכול לומר לו הבן לכהן דעלמא יהביה אבא:
notes.en: Until they tell him: [until people tell] the son that his father instructed at the time of his death that he had not been redeemed. And a statement suffices, without full testimony, because this presumption that he was redeemed is not a strong presumption, as most people do not pay their debt right away. And here one cannot say “until he brings proof,” because here the son can say to the priest: My father gave it to some other priest.

notes.he: לאחר שלשים:
notes.en: Died: after thirty.

notes.he: שיאמרו לו [שלא] נפדה בין עבד בין אשה בין קטן נאמנין:
notes.en: Until they tell him that he was [not] redeemed: whether a slave, a woman or a minor, they are believed.

messages.text: If one had both himself to redeem and his son to redeem, his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son.
The redemption of his son takes precedence, as the mitzva to redeem the father is incumbent upon his own father, and the mitzva to redeem his son is incumbent upon him.

notes.he: מצות פדייתו של אב זה היתה על אביו שמת ומצות בנו עליו:
notes.en: For his mitzva is upon his father: the mitzva of redeeming this father was upon his own father, who has died, and the mitzva of his son is upon him.

messages.text: Gemara
It was stated: In the case of one who redeems his firstborn son within thirty days of his birth by giving a priest five sela coins,
His son is redeemed.
His son is not redeemed.

Everyone agrees that if the father said: He is redeemed from now, that his son is not redeemed, as the obligation to redeem the son is not yet in effect. Likewise, if the father says the redemption should take effect after thirty days, and the money is still there, in the possession of the priest, after thirty days, his son is certainly redeemed, as the money is in the priest’s possession when the obligation of redemption comes into effect.

notes.he: אי אמר ליה מעכשיו יהא בנו פדוי לאו פדיון הוא אלא מתנה בעלמא דהא בתוך שלשים לא שייכא פדייה ואי אמר בתוך ל' הרי לך המעות ולאחר שלשים יחול פדיון בני ואיתנהו מעות ביד כהן בעין לאחר שלשים ודאי פדוי כמאן דיהיב להו ניהליה השתא:
notes.en: Gemara. Everyone agrees: if he said to him, “Let my son be redeemed from now,” it is not a redemption but merely a gift, since within thirty [days] redemption does not apply. And if he said within thirty, “Here is the money for you, and after thirty let the redemption of my son take effect,” and the money is still intact in the priest’s hand after thirty, he is certainly redeemed, as if he had given it to him now.

messages.text: They disagree in a situation where the father says the redemption should take effect after thirty days but the money was squandered away in the meantime.

notes.he: שאינן בעין:
notes.en: Were squandered: they are no longer intact.

messages.text: His son is redeemed, just as is the halakha with regard to the betrothal of a woman on the condition that it takes effect after thirty days. In that case there, is it not correct that even though the money was squandered away during the thirty days it is a valid betrothal?

notes.he: דאי יהיב לה השתא מידי ואמר לה התקדשי לאחר שלשים יום הויא מקודשת כדאמרינן במסכת קדושין (דף נט.):
notes.en: The betrothal of a woman: for if he gives her something now and says to her, “Be betrothed after thirty days,” she is betrothed, as we say in tractate Kiddushin (59a).

notes.he: היכא דאמר לה תקדשי לי לאחר ל' דהויא מקודשת ואע"ג דנתעכלו המעות קודם:
notes.en: Just as with the betrothal of a woman: where he said to her, “Be betrothed to me after thirty [days],” she is betrothed, even though the money was used up beforehand.

notes.he: (כדתרצינן התם):
notes.en: (As we answered there.)

messages.text: Here, too, the halakha is no different.

There, with regard to betrothal, it is in his power to betroth her from now, when he gave her the coins, and therefore it is irrelevant that the money was spent. Conversely, here, in the case of redemption, it is not in his power to redeem his son from now.

notes.he: התם בידו לקדשה מעכשיו אפי' בתוך שלשים הלכך הוו קדושי ואע"ג דנתעכלו המעות:
notes.en: There, it is in his power to betroth her from now, even within thirty; therefore it is a betrothal, even though the money was used up.

messages.text: With regard to the practical halakha in this dispute: And even though we maintain as a principle that wherever Rav and Shmuel disagree the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rav in ritual matters and in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel in monetary matters, here the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, who holds that if one redeems his son within thirty days he is not redeemed.

messages.caption: Redeeming a son before thirty days: where Rav and Shmuel agree, and where they part.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna on the previous amud: If the firstborn son dies within thirty days of birth, although the father gave five sela coins to the priest, the priest must return the five sela coins to him. The Gemara infers: The reason he must return the money is that the son died. But if he did not die within thirty days his son is redeemed despite the fact that the father gave the priest the money prior to the proper time. This inference contradicts the opinion of Shmuel.
messages.quote: dies within thirty days of birth, although the father gave five sela to the priest, the priest must return it

notes.he: הא לא מת בנו פדוי אע"ג דנתן לו קודם:
notes.en: But if he did not die, his son is redeemed, even though he gave it to him beforehand.

messages.text: Here we are dealing with a case where the money is still extant, i.e., in the priest’s possession.

Come and hear another difficulty from the mishna: If the father of the firstborn son dies within thirty days of the birth the presumptive status of the son is that he is not redeemed, until people will tell him that he is redeemed. But if people tell him he is redeemed then the redemption is effective, in contradiction to the opinion of Shmuel.
messages.quote: the presumptive status of the son is that he was not redeemed

notes.he: ממתניתין מת האב בתוך שלשים בחזקת שלא נפדה כו':
notes.en: Come and hear: from our mishna: If the father died within thirty, the presumption is that he was not redeemed, etc.

notes.he: ואי מייתי ראיה הוי פדוי וקשיא לשמואל:
notes.en: We read: “until he brings proof.” And if he brings proof he is redeemed, which is difficult for Shmuel. [The printed Gemara, and the English here, read “until they tell him that he is redeemed.”]

notes.he: הא אמרו לו שנפדה אע"ג דבתוך ל' הוה הוי פדוי:
notes.en: Until they tell him that he was redeemed: so if they told him that he was redeemed, even though it was within thirty, he is redeemed.

messages.text: There too, it is referring to a case where the money is still extant, i.e., in the priest’s possession.
The Gemara relates that a tanna taught a baraita in the presence of Rav Yehuda:
In the case of one who redeems his firstborn son within thirty days of his birth, his son is redeemed.
Shmuel said his son is not redeemed, and yet you say his son is redeemed?

And even though we maintain that the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rav in ritual matters and in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel in monetary matters, here the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel.
§ The mishna teaches that if one had both himself to redeem and his son to redeem, his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son. The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: himself to redeem and his son to redeem, his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son

messages.text: If one had both himself to redeem and his son to redeem, his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son.

The redemption of his son takes precedence, as the mitzva to redeem the father is incumbent upon his own father, and the mitzva to redeem his son is incumbent upon him. Consequently, he should first fulfill the mitzva that is incumbent upon him by redeeming his son.

Everyone concedes that in a case where there are only five sela coins available and one has to redeem both himself and his son, his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son, despite the indication to the contrary from the mishna. What is the reason? The reason is that his own mitzva is preferable to one he performs on behalf of others.
Where they disagree is in a case where there is both land worth five sela coins that is liened property that had been previously sold to others and land worth five sela coins that is unsold property.

Rabbi Yehuda maintains that a loan that is written in the Torah, i.e., a financial obligation by Torah law, such as redemption of the firstborn son with five sela coins, is considered as though it is written in a document, and it can therefore be collected from liened property, as can any loan recorded in a document. Therefore, the five sela coins that are liened property are available for one’s own redemption but not for that of one’s son, as the sale of the property presumably occurred before the birth of his firstborn.

notes.dh: ודידיה אזיל וטריף ממשעבדי ובהני חמש בני חורין פריק ליה לבריה
notes.he: וא"ת היכי טריף ממשעבדי הא אין נפרעין מנכסים משועבדים במקום שיש בני חורין והא איכא חמש בני חורין ואם היה פורק בנו תחלה הוה ניחא וא"ת אכתי ליהדרי לקוחות מהני חמש שפדה כהן בנו דמה נפשך שיעבודם קודם ללידת בנו דאי לידת בנו קדמה אם כן היה יכול לטרוף מן הלקוחות לפדיון בנו כמו לפדיון עצמו וי"ל דהכא מלקוחות שקנו מאביו לפיכך אין חוזרין על הנכסים שקנה הוא ועוד י"ל כגון שלא כתב ללקוחות דאקני והוא קנה הנך חמש בני חרי אחרי כן ואפי' היכא דכתב ליה דאקני בעיא בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קנז.) אבל היכא דלא כתב ליה קיימא לן דלא משתעבד ואם תאמר אי הנך משעבדי בנכסים שקנה מאביו ניחא אבל בנכסים שקנה הוא היכי משתעבדי לפדיונו דהא אימת חל חיוב פדיון עצמו כשהביא שתי שערות שנעשה גדול תו לא אשתעבד נכסים שקנה אחרי כן דלא כתב ליה לכהן דאיקני וצריך לומר דעל כרחין מיירי כשירש מאביו מיהו לר' יהודה נמי זימנין דמשכחת לההוא קודם לבנו כגון שאין לו נכסים מאביו ומשהביא שערות קנה הני קרקעות ומכרם לאחר לידת בנו דלפדיון בנו אזיל וטריף ממשעבדי ועוד י"ל דנכסים שקנה אחרי כן חל עלייהו שיעבוד לענין פדיון ואע"ג דלא כתב דאיקני דכל שעתא ושעתא רכיב עליה חיוב פדיון וכיון דחשבינן ליה כמלוה בשטר הוי כאילו נכתב לאחר שקנה הקרקעות:
notes.en: In brief: [On “For his own he goes and seizes from liened property, and with these five unencumbered ones he redeems his son.”] Tosafot ask: how can the priest seize liened property, when one does not collect from liened property where there is unencumbered property, and here there are five unencumbered? Had he redeemed his son first, it would be fine. And further: let the buyers then come back and take the five with which the priest redeemed the son, since either way their lien came before the son’s birth, for had the birth come first, the priest could seize from the buyers for the son as for the father. They answer that the buyers here bought from his father, so they cannot turn to property he himself acquired; or that the buyers’ deed did not say “what I shall acquire” [de’akni], and he acquired these unencumbered five afterward. (Even where de’akni was written it is a question in Mi SheMet, Bava Batra 157a; without it, we hold later property is not liened.) They then ask: if the sold land came from his father, fine; but how can land he himself acquired be liened for his own redemption, when that obligation took effect only when he came of age, and later acquisitions are not liened to the priest without de’akni? It must therefore speak of land he inherited from his father. Yet even for Rabbi Yehuda the son’s redemption can sometimes come first, as where he had nothing from his father, bought the land after coming of age and sold it after his son’s birth: then for his son’s redemption he goes and seizes from liened property. Alternatively, later acquisitions are liened for redemption even without de’akni, since the obligation rests on him at every moment, and since it counts as a loan written in a document, it is as if the document were written after he acquired the land. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: And therefore the priest goes and repossesses the land worth five sela that is liened property for his own redemption, like any debt written in a document; and with those five sela of unsold property he redeems his son. In this manner, one can fulfill both mitzvot.

notes.he: חמש סלעים דידיה אזיל כהן וטריף ממשעבדי שהרי שיעבודו של כהן קדם והיינו דקאמר שמצותו על אביו כלומר שמאביו נשתעבדו אותן נכסים לכהן:
notes.en: And his own: for his own five sela the priest goes and seizes from liened property, since the priest’s lien came first. That is what [the mishna] says, “for his mitzva is upon his father”: that is, those properties became liened to the priest from his father’s time.

notes.dh: ובהנך חמש בני חרי פריק לבניה
notes.he: מיד דאי יהיב בני חרי משום פדיון דידיה תו לא מיפריק בנו דשמא שיעבוד הלקוחות קודם ללידת בנו:
notes.en: And with these five unencumbered ones he redeems his son: right away. For if he gave the unencumbered ones for his own redemption, his son could no longer be redeemed, since perhaps the buyers’ lien came before his son’s birth.

messages.text: And the Rabbis maintain: A loan that is written in the Torah is not considered as though it is written in a document, since buyers will not know to guard against repossession if it is not written in a document. Therefore, the five sela coins that are liened property are not available for redemption, and consequently his own mitzva is preferable. He accordingly redeems himself with the land that is not liened.

notes.he: ואי יהיב בני חרי בשביל פדיון בנו תו לא מיפריק איהו דכהן לא מצי טריף לקוחות:
notes.en: Is not like one written in a document: so if he gave the unencumbered ones for his son’s redemption, he himself could no longer be redeemed, since the priest cannot seize from the buyers.

notes.he: ולא גבי ממשעבדי וליכא אלא ה' בני חורין:
notes.en: Is not like one written in a document: so he does not collect from liened property, and there are only the five unencumbered.

messages.caption: Rabbi Yirmeya: with only five sela the father redeems himself; with five in sold land and five in unsold land, Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis part ways.

messages.text: Mishna

The five sela coins of the redemption of the firstborn son, with regard to which it is written: “Five shekels of silver, after the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Numbers 18:16), are calculated using a Tyrian maneh. The silver content of the Tyrian coinage is significantly higher than that of provincial coinage, which is worth one-eighth its value.

verse.he: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verse.en: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Mishna. A Tyrian maneh: this is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: אשם בכסף שקלים וערכין לא איצטריך ליה לתנא למיתני דבאשם כתיב בהדיא בשקל הקדש וערכין נמי פשיטא דבשקל הקדש הוו כיון דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ה) וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש:
notes.en: The five sela of the son, etc.: The tanna did not need to teach the guilt offering of silver shekels or valuations [in this list], for with the guilt offering it is written explicitly “in the shekel of the Sanctuary,” and valuations too are obviously in the shekel of the Sanctuary, since it is written: “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25).

messages.text: With regard to the thirty shekels paid to the owner of a Canaanite slave who is killed by an ox (see Exodus 21:32), and the fifty shekels paid by a rapist (see Deuteronomy 22:29) and by a seducer (see Exodus 22:16) of a young virgin woman, and the one hundred shekels paid by the defamer of his bride with the claim that she is not a virgin (see Deuteronomy 22:19),

notes.he: כלומר וכן חמשים של אונס וכו':
notes.en: Fifty of the rapist and of the seducer: that is, and likewise the fifty of the rapist, etc.

messages.text: all of them, even those cases where the word shekel is not explicitly written, are paid in the shekel of the Sanctuary, whose value is twenty gera (see Numbers 18:16) and that is calculated using a Tyrian maneh.

notes.he: דהוו עשרין מעין ואותן מעין שבמעות מנה צורי. ובגמ' מפרש למה לי למיהדר ולמיתני האי וכו':
notes.en: All of them in the shekel of the Sanctuary: which is twenty ma’a, and those ma’a are of the coinage of the Tyrian maneh. The Gemara explains why the tanna needed to go back and teach this, etc.

messages.text: And all monetary obligations are redeemed, i.e., paid, with coins or with items of the equivalent value of money, except for the half-shekels that are donated to the Temple each year, which must be given specifically as coins.

notes.he: שקלים הבאים בלשכה באדר אין מביאין שם אלא מטבע של חצי שקלים:
notes.en: Except for shekels: the shekels brought to the chamber in Adar; one brings there only coins of half-shekels.

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna stated that the five sela coins of the redemption of the son are calculated using a Tyrian maneh.
One must give five sela of the maneh used in Tyre.

notes.he: היוצא במדינת צורי דהסלע ד' זוזים והזוז במשקל זהב של משקל שני פשיטין ומחצה למשקל הברזל:
notes.en: Gemara. The maneh of Tyre: the one current in the province of Tyre, whose sela is four zuz, and the zuz is the weight of a gold coin weighing two and a half pshitin by iron weight.

notes.dh: אמר רבי אסי מנה של צורי
notes.he: פי' בקונט' היוצא במדינת צור וזהו שיעור סלע של אותו מנה דבסלע ד' זוזים והזוז כמשקל זהוב של משקל שני פשיטים ומחצה למשקל הברזל ונראה שקבלה היתה בידו מרבותיו ומשמע שרוצה לומר דזוז הוא דינר של כסף ומשקלו של זהב וכמו כן פירש בפי' חומש בפרשת ואלה המשפטים גבי ל' שקל דהשקל משקלו ארבעה זהובים שהם חצי אונקיי"א למשקל הישר של קלונייא משמע נמי שרוצה לומר דדינר כסף וזהב משקלו שוה דסלע הוא ד' דינרים אבל לא נראה לר"ת מדקאמר דדינר של זהב משקלו כשנים של כסף כמו שאפרש בסמוך ועוד פי' בקונט' דר' חנינא דאמר איסתירא סרסיא דמזבנא תמניא מינייהו בדינרא היינו בדינר האמור בכל הש"ס הוא דינר שמינית שבדינר צורי ור' חנינא תנא הוא ופליג אמתניתין והשתא הוו חמש סלעים דבר מועט מאי דקאמר חמשה מינייהו לפדיון הבן ותמניא מינייהו לא שוו אלא שמינית שבדינר צורי וצורי גופיה אין משקלו אלא שני פשיטים ומחצה נמצא דחמש סלעים של בן אין שוין פשוט אחד ממטבע שלנו לר' חנינא ועוד דדינר מפרש דהוא דינר מדינה ובלשון משנה רגיל לקרותו זוז ובלשון הש"ס רגיל לקרותו פשיטי כי ההוא דכתובות (דף סז.) דאמרינן חמשי זוזי פשיטי ועוד בכל דוכתי בסתם דינרא הוה דדהבא דמזדבנא בעשרים וחמשה זוזי בפ"ק דקדושין (דף מ.) גבי רב כהנא דיהיב ליה אליהו שייפא דדינרי ור' אמי דאשכח אונייא דדינרי כלומר בדינרין זהב ונראה לפרש דכולהו לא פליגי ואמתני' קיימי לפרושי לן שיעורא דר' אמי מנה צורי כלומר סלעים ה' סלעים ממנה של סלעים של בן:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi explains Rabbi Asi’s “maneh of Tyre” as the one current in Tyre, whose sela is four zuz, each zuz the weight of a gold coin of two and a half pshitin by iron weight. He seems to have had this as a tradition from his teachers, and it implies that a silver dinar weighs the same as a gold one, as he also explains on the Torah (Mishpatim, the thirty shekels) that the shekel weighs four gold coins, half an ounce by the true weight of Cologne. Rabbeinu Tam disagrees, since a gold dinar weighs as much as two silver ones, as explained below. Rashi also explains that Rabbi Ḥanina’s Syrian sela, eight to a dinar, refers to the ordinary dinar of the Talmud, an eighth of the Tyrian dinar, and that Rabbi Ḥanina is a Tanna who disagrees with the mishna. But then the five sela would be a trifle: eight of them worth an eighth of a Tyrian dinar, itself only two and a half pshitin, so that for Rabbi Ḥanina the five sela of the son would not be worth one pashut of our coinage. Further, Rashi takes the dinar as a provincial dinar, which the Mishna usually calls zuz and the Talmud pshiti (as in Ketubot 67a, “fifty zuz pshiti”), whereas everywhere an unqualified dinara is gold, sold for twenty-five zuz, as in Kiddushin (40a), where Elijah gave Rav Kahana a bundle of dinars, and Rabbi Ami found a ship of dinars, meaning gold dinars. It seems better to explain that none of them disagree, and all come to explain the measure of the mishna: “Tyrian maneh” means five sela from a maneh of sela, the sela of the son. [The text here names Rabbi Ami.] Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: מנה של צור כ"ה שקלים במנה של תורה:
notes.en: The maneh of Tyre: twenty-five shekels to the maneh of the Torah.

messages.text: The five sela coins are equal to a golden Arabian dinar.

notes.he: סלע צורי היינו דינר ערבא ישמעאלי. ולא פירש לי שיעורו ומצאתי בתשובת הגאונים בבליים ששבעה דינרים האמורים בכל הש"ס שהדינר שש מעה כסף עושין עשרה מאותן של ערביא ובלשון ערבי קורין אותה מגרעות:
notes.en: Rabbi Ami says: the Tyrian sela is the Arabian, Ishmaelite, dinar. [My teacher] did not explain its measure to me, but I found in a responsum of the Babylonian Geonim that seven of the dinars mentioned throughout the Talmud, the dinar being six silver ma’a, make ten of those of Arabia; and in Arabic they call it migra’ot.

notes.he: כלומר דינר של ערביא שוה ה' סלעים של בן ולא כמו שפי' בקונט' דסלע צורי דינרא ערביא וגם פירש שמצאתי בתשובת הגאונים של בבליים ששבעה דינרים האמורים בכ"מ בהש"ס שהדינר שש מעה כסף עושין עשרה מאותו של ערביא ודבריו סותרין זה את זה דכיון דדינר של ערביא קטן אפילו מדינר שבכל הש"ס אין יכול להיות דסלע צורי הוא דינר ערביא והלא בסלע ד' דינרי מאותם של צורי שבכל הש"ס כדאמרינן בקדושין ובכל דוכתי אלא בדינרי זהב איירי ושל ערביא קטן הוא מדינר זהב של צורי דשל צור מיזדבן בכ"ה של כסף ושל ערביא בעשרים כדפרישית דשיעורו כה' סלעים של בן:
notes.en: Rabbi Ami says: An Arabian dinar: that is, an Arabian dinar is worth five sela of the son; not as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained, that the Tyrian sela is the Arabian dinar. He also wrote, “I found in a responsum of the Babylonian Geonim that seven of the dinars mentioned throughout the Talmud, the dinar being six silver ma’a, make ten of those of Arabia,” and his words contradict each other. Since the Arabian dinar is smaller even than the dinar of the Talmud, the Tyrian sela cannot be the Arabian dinar, for a sela holds four of the Tyrian dinars mentioned throughout the Talmud, as we say in Kiddushin and everywhere. Rather, [Rabbi Ami] speaks of gold dinars, and the Arabian one is smaller than the Tyrian gold dinar, for the Tyrian is sold for twenty-five silver [dinars] and the Arabian for twenty, as I explained: its measure is that of the five sela of the son.

notes.he: נמי הוי סלע:
notes.en: Rabbi Ami says: An Arabian dinar: this too is a sela.

messages.text: There is a Syrian sela [istera], eight of which are sold for a large golden dinar. One must give five of these for the redemption of the son.

notes.he: סלעים מיושנים:
notes.en: Istera susarita: old sela coins.

notes.he: מינייהו בדינרא:
notes.en: Eight of which are sold: eight of them for a dinar.

notes.he: כן כתוב ברוב ספרים אבל בקונטרס פירש סווסריתא נראה דבין זה ובין זה נקרא על שם סוריא כמו (ב"ק דף פג.) לשון סורסי שהוא על סוריא והוא סלע של סוריא דמזדבנא תמני בדינרא היינו בדינר זהב של סוריא וגדול הוא מדינר זהב של צור שבכל הש"ס דהסוריא לא מיזדבן בעשרים וחמש והאי של סוריא ששוה שמונה של בן היינו שלשים ושנים דינר של כסף שהסלע ארבעה דינרין:
notes.en: Rabbi Ḥanina says: Istera sesuraya: so it is written in most texts, but the Kuntres [Rashi] reads susarita. It seems both are named for Syria, as in Bava Kamma (83a) the word sursi refers to Syria. It is a Syrian sela, eight of which are sold for a dinar, that is, for a Syrian gold dinar, which is larger than the Tyrian gold dinar mentioned throughout the Talmud, since the Syrian is not sold for twenty-five. And this Syrian dinar, worth eight [sela] of the son, is thirty-two silver dinars, since the sela is four dinars.

notes.he: סלע של אותו מקום שהן קלים שנותנין מהן ח' בדינר של זהב. דינר זהב הוי ה' פשוט למשקל הברזל דינר כסף ב' ומחצה למשקל הברזל ודינו דינר זהב בסלעים דאורייתא אין דינו לימכר אלא בו' סלעים של כסף שהן כ"ד דינרי כסף שהן כ"ד זוז (והאי זוז דינר האי) והאי דקאמר ר' יוחנן כ"ה זוז אותו זוז נכנס להכרע כ"ד זוזין אם היו שוקלין כל אחד לבד:
notes.en: Istera sursaya: a sela of that place; they are light, so that eight of them are given for a gold dinar. A gold dinar is five pshitin by iron weight, a silver dinar two and a half by iron weight. And the rule of a gold dinar in Torah sela: it is to be sold only for six silver sela, which are twenty-four silver dinars, which are twenty-four zuz. And when Rabbi Yoḥanan [50a] says twenty-five zuz, that [extra] zuz goes to tip the scale for the twenty-four zuz, if each were weighed by itself.

notes.he: כלומר שהוא כסרסור שבו עושין כל סחורה. למ"ה:
notes.en: Another version: sursaya, that is, it is like a broker [sarsur], with which all trade is done. [The note ends with an unclear abbreviation.]

messages.text: The reckoning of the five sela continues on 50a, with Rabbi Yoḥanan’s worn gold dinars of Hadrian and Trajan.
